svg.text: POISONING IN A CHILD — WHAT NOT TO DO MATTERS MOST
NEVER MAKE A CHILD VOMIT — NOT SALT WATER, NOT PALM OIL, NOT A FINGER IN THE THROAT
WHY VOMITING HARMS
Kerosene and petrol are thin and slippery. Brought
back up they run into the lungs and cause a chemical
pneumonitis that is far worse than the swallowed dose.
Caustic soda, bleach and acid burn the oesophagus
once going down and a second time coming back up.
WHAT TO DO INSTEAD
Airway, breathing, circulation first — always
Wipe the mouth; remove contaminated clothing
Wash skin or irrigate eyes with running water
Nothing by mouth; position on the side if drowsy
Transfer at once and keep the child warm
BRING THE CONTAINER
Send the bottle, sachet, leaves or tablets with the child. The name and strength of the substance,
the amount missing and the time it was taken decide the treatment. A guess does not.
PREVENTION — TEACH IT AT EVERY CHILD WELFARE CLINIC
Never store kerosene or weedicide in a drinks bottle. A child trusts a familiar bottle.
Keep medicines, bleach and paraffin locked or high up, out of sight as well as out of reach.
Most childhood poisoning happens in the home, in the second year of life, while someone is nearby.
